thread:
maria: Nightly perf alert, p95 up ~30% for small-seq chat workload in us-west around 03:12. Dashboard shows sustained delta starting at 02:50. :eyes:
ci-bot: nightly-bench job #56321 failed: p95_increase=29.7% (ref: master@6f2a3c) https://ci.internal/b/56321
raj: I merged adaptive-eviction-smoother (PR #5428) last night around 01:40 — could be related. It changes the KV eviction smoothing window and bumping the kernel-selection fallback threshold.
olivia: quick local microbench with --seq-len=32 and --batch=8 reproduces p95 regression. baseline (pre-PR) p95=118ms, post-PR p95=154ms. CPU profile shows extra time in kv_cache::evict_range and a new branch in kernel_selector::should_fallback
henry: can someone paste the flame or perf log? I'm thinking the smoother is causing thrash where we prematurely drop prefixes, causing more cold kernel paths and smaller batches.
olivia: paste of simplified perf timeline:
```
00:00.000 request start
00:00.012 kv hit
00:00.020 kv eviction triggered (smoothing=true)
00:00.038 kernel select -> fallback to generic_kernel
00:00.042 run generic_kernel (no fused attention)
00:00.156 finish
```
maria: that fallback window aligns with the PR change that lowers the batch-coalescing threshold when eviction rate > X. If smoothing delays eviction a bit, we might get more eviction bursts later.
raj: I pushed a quick patch that reverts the lowering of the fallback threshold (branch: revert/eviction-threshold). Can we run the nightly-bench compare between master and revert branch?
ci-bot: queued diff bench between master@6f2a3c and revert/eviction-threshold (job #56328). ETA ~20m.
olivia: also ran an instrumented run that logs batch sizes & kernel choices; snippet below:
```
batch_sizes: [1,1,2,1,1,3,1]
kernel_choices: [fast_kernel, fast_kernel, generic_kernel, fast_kernel, generic_kernel, generic_kernel, fast_kernel]
```
henry: small batches + intermittent generic kernel -> explains p95 jump. Looks like eviction produces short-lived cache holes that break batching coalescing windows.
maria: proposed next steps:
- wait for diff bench (#56328)
- if revert fixes, roll back the threshold change and rework smoothing logic (less bursty)
- add unit/integration test that simulates eviction bursts and asserts batch coalescing behavior
- add a perf regression alert to correlate p95 spikes with kernel_fallback_rate metric
raj: agreed. adding test now. If bench confirms revert fixes, I'll open a revert PR and coordinate a quick roll-forward after we fix smoothing.
ci-bot: diff bench complete: p95 delta between master and revert branch -> -27.5% (revert is better). job #56328 details: https://ci.internal/b/56328
maria: ok let's revert. raj can you open the revert PR and mark it rollback-critical? I'll trigger the rollback once PR passes smoke. :+1:
olivia: filed PR #5437 (revert: restore fallback threshold). Triggering canary.
henry: also adding a dashboard panel for kernel_fallback_rate and kv_eviction_burst_count so we catch similar regressions earlier.
maria: thanks everyone. tagging postmortem if rollback goes green.
ci-bot: deploy canary started for PR #5437 (canary-3 nodes). monitor: canary/5437/status
